content:
Alex: Heads-up — I think I found a JS SDK bug around cursor pagination + client-side throttling. Reproducer in sample-app branch.
Marisa: What are you seeing? any logs or steps to repro?
Alex: Steps: run paginate-e2e with concurrency=20 and client throttle at 50rps, short token TTL so refresh happens mid-run. Behavior: when token refresh happens, the JS SDK appears to replay the current page request immediately and ignores server Retry-After / X-RateLimit-Reset headers, which causes duplicate page fetches and the in-process queue spikes.
Sasha: Which SDK version? does Go behave differently?
Alex: js-sdk v0.8.4. Go SDK v0.8.4 behaves correctly (respects Retry-After and schedules backoff). Logs excerpt:
```
[2026-02-15T14:06:12Z] req=abc123 -> 429
headers: Retry-After: 3, X-RateLimit-Reset: 167665
[2026-02-15T14:06:12Z] token: refreshing (expired)
[2026-02-15T14:06:12Z] js-sdk retry middleware: immediate retry queued for req=abc123
[2026-02-15T14:06:12Z] go-sdk: scheduled retry for req=abc123 at +3s
```
Priya: Interesting — sounds like token refresh path is interfering with retry middleware. Maybe the JS flow cancels the inflight promise then re-enqueues it without consulting headers.
Alex: Here's the minimal bad pattern in our client middleware:
```
// pseudo
await refreshTokenIfNeeded();
// then re-run request() unconditionally
return this._dispatch(req);
```
If refreshTokenIfNeeded triggers while retry middleware already saw 429 and parsed Retry-After, we end up issuing an extra immediate dispatch.
Marisa: Does this only affect cursor pagination or streaming endpoints too?
Alex: So far observed with cursor pagination in paginate-e2e. Streaming endpoints don't duplicate tokens the same way, but electron sample app shows a memory spike when pagination duplicates happen because the local queue grows.
Sasha: Can you open a tiny repro and a PR with a failing e2e test? We should modify the JS retry middleware to honor server headers and make the token refresh path preserve the intended backoff schedule (i.e., don't immediate-requeue if a retry is already scheduled).
Alex: PR opened: github.com/redwood/sample-apps#fix-js-retry-1234 with reproducer and a test that simulates token expiry mid-pagination.
devex-bot: Deploy preview created for PR #1234 — e2e job started; electron sample failing with memory spike.
Priya: For the electron issue, we probably need both fixes: header-aware retry and a bounded request queue with dedupe by idempotency/request-id so duplicates are dropped. The current client queue is unbounded and gets filled when duplicates are emitted.
Marisa: Agreed. Action items: 1) patch retry middleware to honor Retry-After and X-RateLimit-Reset, 2) make token-refresh not re-enqueue inflight requests (or keep the original scheduled retry), 3) add optional bounded queue + dedupe key for sample apps, 4) add docs note about recommended token TTL > pagination window for heavy cursor workloads. Assign to Sasha and Alex for quick patch.
Sasha: Taking it — will submit patch + unit tests today. I'll also add a small integration test that simulates the RT refresh + 429 headers at scale.
Alex: Thanks — I left the reproducer and the logs in sample-app branch `js/retry-patch-repro`. Also added a minimal electron repro that shows mem growth when duplicates are pushed.
Marisa: Nice. Once patches land, let's run a full throttling soak (24h) against our hosted test model to validate.
Alex: Sounds good. Will follow up with PR links and test matrix results here.
Marisa: :thumbsup:
Alex: Thanks everyone — removing my debug logs from main branch after PR merges.
